newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end lower before holiday break.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end lower before holiday break.

text.p: Swedish debt yields ended lower on Monday with rates at the short end falling heavily during morning trade but longer maturities only slipping a little.
"The fall in short maturities is temporary. It might be hard to find a reasonable placement over the year-end," one dealer said.
One of Sweden's major banks was buying T-bills during morning trade, boosting the market, another dealer said.
"There is not much happening and the focus is Christmas now," one dealer said.
The six-month T-bill rate fell six basis points to 3.82 percent and the ten year bond yield dropped one basis point to 6.75 percent.
The spread between German and Swedish long yields fell two basis points to 94.
The crown weakened a touch to 4.4035 crowns against the mark against 4.3900 late Friday.
The debt and currency markets closed at 1100 GMT, to reopen on Friday.
